Force-directed SFDP layout and breadth-first search traversal

sfdp_layout.Rd

sfdp_layout() computes a two-dimensional spring-electrical force-directed layout in native C++ following Hu (2005) and graph-tool's sfdp_layout(), using exact pairwise repulsion for small graphs (\(N \le 128\)) and a Barnes-Hut quadtree for larger graphs.

graph_bfs() computes a breadth-first search traversal and shortest-path spanning tree from source up to depth max_dist.

Usage

sfdp_layout(graph, pos = NULL, C = 0.2, K = 1.0, p = 2.0, theta = 0.6,
  gamma = 1.0, mu = 0.0, mu_p = 1.0, init_step = NULL, cooling_step = 0.95,
  max_level = 10L, tol = 1e-4, max_iter = 200L, simple = FALSE,
  groups = NULL, pin = NULL)

graph_bfs(graph, source, max_dist = Inf, directed = NULL)

Arguments

graph

A graph created by graph_create.

pos

Optional \(N \times 2\) numeric matrix of initial vertex coordinates. Useful for warm-starting or incremental layout updates (max_iter = 1L).

C

Relative repulsive force strength (positive scalar).

K

Optimal spring length (positive scalar).

p

Repulsive force exponent (positive scalar; default 2.0).

theta

Barnes-Hut quadtree opening angle parameter (used when \(N > 128\) and max_level > 0).

gamma

Inter-group force coefficient (> 0 attracts distinct groups toward each other, < 0 repels them).

mu

Intra-group attractive force coefficient (>= 0).

mu_p

Intra-group attractive scaling exponent.

init_step

Optional positive initial displacement step size. Defaults to max(K, 0.1 * K * sqrt(N)).

cooling_step

Multiplicative step-size cooling factor in (0, 1].

max_level

Maximum Barnes-Hut quadtree depth (integer >= 0).

tol

Stopping tolerance on mean vertex displacement relative to K.

max_iter

Maximum number of layout iterations (0L means no cap).

simple

Logical; if TRUE, use monotone cooling (step <- step * cooling_step); if FALSE, use Hu (2005) adaptive step sizing.

groups

Optional vector of length \(N\) assigning vertices to groups for inter- and intra-group layout forces.

pin

Optional logical vector of length \(N\); vertices with TRUE remain fixed at their initial pos coordinates.

source

1-based integer index of the starting vertex for BFS.

max_dist

Maximum BFS depth (Inf for unrestricted traversal, or a non-negative integer).

directed

Logical or NULL. If NULL, defaults to isTRUE(graph$directed).

Details

Both functions are deterministic given R's random number seed (set.seed for sfdp_layout(), and completely deterministic for graph_bfs()). Self-loops are ignored during layout and BFS traversal; parallel edges are collapsed to a single tree edge in graph_bfs().

Value

sfdp_layout() returns an \(N \times 2\) numeric matrix with column names "x" and "y".

graph_bfs() returns an object of class "rgraphtool_bfs" with elements source, max_dist, directed, distance (numeric vector of length \(N\), Inf for unreached vertices), parent (integer vector of 1-based predecessors, NA_integer_ for the source and unreached vertices), order (1-based discovery order), and tree_edges (logical vector aligned with graph_edges).

Examples

g <- graph_create(10L, directed = FALSE)
graph_add_edges(g, cbind(1:9, 2:10))
set.seed(1)
pos <- sfdp_layout(g, max_iter = 40L)
bfs <- graph_bfs(g, source = 1L, max_dist = 3L)
print(bfs)
#> rgraphtool BFS traversal
#>   source: 1 (undirected, max_dist = 3)
#>   reached: 4 / 10 vertices (max distance = 3, tree edges = 3)
